title: Equity Overview 'Insiders' shows 51.18% for a bank that has zero promoter/insider holding
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/DHANBANK -> held_percent_insiders: 0.51176 (rendered as 'Insiders' in the Ownership section, src/modules/equity-overview/EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:141). Both screener.in and groww.in's shareholding tables for DHANBANK carry NO Promoters/insiders row at all -- Dhanlaxmi Bank is a promoter-less, widely-held old-generation private bank (screener.in shareholding table shows only FII 14.21% / DII 0.05% / Public 85.74-85.75%, confirmed independently by groww.in). The app's own /disclosures/shareholding?symbol=DHANBANK (the BSE-XBRL-sourced endpoint) agrees, returning promoter_percent: null for all 12 quarters on file -- so the app has correct data for the same fact sitting right next to the wrong one.
evidence: src/modules/equity-overview/EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:141 (label 'Insiders', key held_percent_insiders, kind 'fraction'); sidecar/services/yfinance_provider.py:398 (held_percent_insiders=_num(info.get('heldPercentInsiders')), no correction applied); sidecar/services/correctness_gate.py:198-224 (_apply_plausibility_bounds only withholds held_percent_insiders when it falls OUTSIDE [0,1] -- 0.51176 is a syntactically valid fraction so it passes through untouched, field_meta stays status='ok'); sidecar/services/ownership_check.py:1-33 (a purpose-built NSE/BSE cross-check exists specifically for this yfinance failure mode -- its own docstring documents 'heldPercentInsiders overstates the NSE/BSE promoter-group percentage by 3.5-5.4pp on several NSE names', i.e. the mechanism was built for single-digit drift, not a 51-point fabrication for a promoter-less issuer -- but per ownership_check.py's module docstring the check is wired only into the RESEARCH snapshot builder's fundamentals leg (services.research.semantics.derive_semantics), never into the plain GET /fundamentals/<symbol> route the Equity Overview panel and sidecar/services/company_narrative.py both call directly (company_narrative.py:177-178 explicitly folds held_percent_insiders into the SAME numeric-verification set used to legitimize the AI narrative's claims -- an LLM sentence citing 'insiders hold 51%' would pass verification as a real, sourced number).
notes: Principle violated: a correction mechanism was purpose-built for exactly this yfinance failure class but is wired into only one of two consumers of the same raw fundamentals -- the panel a user actually reads bypasses it entirely. Concrete consequence: any DHANBANK viewer sees a fabricated 51% 'insider' ownership figure for a bank that literally has none, and if they ask the AI narrative to summarize ownership, the false figure would be treated as independently verified. Smallest fix shape: route the plain /fundamentals/<symbol> response (or at minimum EquityOverviewPanel's render path) through the same ownership_check.get_exchange_ownership cross-check the research leg already has, or apply a coarser plausibility rule in correctness_gate.py that withholds held_percent_insiders when the app's own /disclosures/shareholding for the same symbol shows promoter_percent=null/0 and the yfinance figure diverges by more than a few points.

title: No quarterly results/income surface at all -- the just-published Q1 FY2026-27 numbers are invisible in-app
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/DHANBANK/income (and /balance, /cashflow) -> periods: ['2026','2025','2024','2023'] -- annual only, no quarterly breakdown, no route accepts a quarterly parameter (sidecar/routers/fundamentals.py:177-188 has exactly one income/balance/cashflow route each, unparametrized). Outside truth: DHANBANK's board approved and screener.in already carries the Q1 FY2026-27 (quarter ended 2026-06-30) results -- interest earned Rs 449 cr, net profit Rs 25 cr (+108% YoY vs Rs 12 cr a year earlier), EPS Rs 0.63. The app's own schema anticipates quarterly-derived growth (Fundamentals.revenue_growth_computed / earnings_growth_computed / growth_computed_quarters, sidecar/models/fundamentals.py:119-122) but all three came back null for DHANBANK in this collection.
evidence: sidecar/routers/fundamentals.py:177-188 (income/balance/cashflow routes, no quarterly variant); collected calls 'income'/'balance'/'cashflow' in docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P12_DHANBANK.json (periods arrays are fiscal years 2023-2026 only); sidecar/models/fundamentals.py:119-122 (revenue_growth_computed, earnings_growth_computed, growth_computed_quarters fields exist in the contract, all null in the collected fundamentals body); sidecar/services/yfinance_provider.py:172-178 (_DERIVED_FIELDS names these as populated by 'the research derived leg', i.e. a mechanism separate from the plain fundamentals fetch)
notes: Principle violated: a screener.in-grade product benchmark explicitly names quarterly results as core coverage (COMMON.md brief), and for an Indian small-cap bank quarterly EPS/NII swings ARE the headline signal (Q1FY27 net profit +108% YoY is exactly the kind of move a demanding user needs surfaced, not buried behind an annual-only statement). Smallest fix shape: either wire the same quarterly-growth derived leg that already exists in the schema into the plain fundamentals fetch (so it is not research-pipeline-only), or add a quarterly income/balance route backed by the same source that already feeds results_calendar's board-meeting dates.

title: Confirmed-zero trailing dividend renders as an unexplained blank, not an affirmed 0
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/DHANBANK -> dividend_per_share_ttm: null, dividend_yield: null. Outside truth (screener.in) states the dividend payout has been 0% in EVERY fiscal year it publishes, Mar-2015 through Mar-2026 -- a definite, sourced zero, not an unknown ('Though the company is reporting repeated profits, it is not paying out dividend').
evidence: sidecar/services/yfinance_provider.py:172-178 (dividend_per_share_ttm listed in _DERIVED_FIELDS, populated only by 'the research derived leg: trailing-12m dividends'); collected fundamentals body in docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P12_DHANBANK.json (dividend_yield: null, dividend_per_share: null, dividend_per_share_ttm: null, all three)
notes: Principle violated: the same research-only-wiring pattern as DAT-P12-1/DAT-P12-2 -- a derived/affirmed-zero mechanism exists in the model contract but the plain fundamentals fetch the panel reads never runs it, so 'confirmed no dividend' and 'we don't know' render identically (a blank dash). Smallest fix shape: run the trailing-12m-dividend derivation (or at minimum, affirmatively stamp 0 when the provider's raw dividend fields are absent AND the income history shows no dividend line) on the plain fundamentals path, not only inside the research snapshot.

title: Resolver has no former-name data; searching the bank's documented pre-2010 legal name ranks a dead ghost instrument above the real bank
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/resolve?q=Dhanalakshmi+Bank (fresh fetch, 2026-09-23, isolated sidecar) -> needs_disambiguation: true, candidates[0] = {symbol: 'DHAN-RE', name: 'Dhanlaxmi Bank Ltd', exchange: 'BSE', confidence: 0.7429, bse_code: '750942'} ranked ABOVE candidates[1] = {symbol: 'DHANBANK', confidence: 0.6667, bse_code: '532180'}, the actual listed, trading bank. DHAN-RE is the January-2025 Rights Entitlement (ISIN INE680A20011) -- an expired, non-trading line with no price, exactly the 'ghost instrument' the pack flags as a trap. Every candidate in every resolve response for this entity (resolve_bare_symbol, resolve_company_name, resolve_bse_code, and this fresh former-name query) carries former_name: null, confirming the resolver never populated the field despite the bank's well-documented 2010-08-10 rename from 'Dhanalakshmi Bank' to 'Dhanlaxmi Bank' (and a third spelling, 'Dhanalaxmi', in the issuer's own current annual-report filename).
evidence: collected 'resolve_company_name' call in docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P12_DHANBANK.json (former_name: null on every candidate); fresh GET /resolve?q=Dhanalakshmi+Bank on 2026-09-23 against http://127.0.0.1:52152 (candidates[0].symbol='DHAN-RE' confidence 0.7429 > candidates[1].symbol='DHANBANK' confidence 0.6667, former_name null on both)
notes: Principle violated: a symbol resolver that ranks fuzzy-name matches needs the entity's alias history to rank correctly, and this is a live, reproducible failure mode, not a hypothetical -- a user typing the bank's own former legal name is handed a dead rights-entitlement instrument as the TOP candidate. Smallest fix shape: populate former_name (and the 'Dhanalaxmi' filename-spelling alias) in the resolver's name index for this entity, and/or down-weight or exclude expired/delisted rights-entitlement lines (asset class or a 'delisted'/'expired' flag) from fuzzy company-name ranking generally.

title: Face value has no field anywhere in the app's data contract
repro: grep -rn "face_value" types/data.ts sidecar/models/fundamentals.py -> no matches. Outside truth: face value INR 10.0, cross-checked arithmetically (equity capital Rs 395 cr / 39.47 cr shares = Rs 10.01) and first-party (Letter of Offer rights price 'Rs. 21.00 including a premium of Rs.11.00' implies Rs 10 face value).
evidence: types/data.ts (no face_value key); sidecar/models/fundamentals.py (no face_value field); collected fundamentals body in docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P12_DHANBANK.json (39 keys enumerated, none named face_value)
notes: Principle violated: face value is a standard Indian-equity per-share fact (needed to sanity-check bonus/split ratios and rights-issue premiums, both directly relevant to this entity's own 14:25 rights issue at Rs 21 = Rs 10 face + Rs 11 premium) and is entirely absent from the data model, not just unpopulated for this symbol. Smallest fix shape: add a face_value field to the Fundamentals model, sourced from the same provider info snapshot (yfinance often omits it for Indian names, so this may need a screener-style secondary source or a derived shares-outstanding/equity-capital identity where available).
